explicit_cautions: Do not give the dead legitimate child no individuality; portray him as a real person before the accident.
Do not make infertility or jealousy the sole motive for Victoria's subsequent decisions.
Do not reduce the younger mother to a reproductive plot device; she must have her own agency.
Do not assert Victoria murdered Julian's mother without deliberate later authorization; preserve genuine ambiguity.
Do not make Julian's later politics genetically or psychologically inevitable, or predetermine his character.
Preserve Victoria's independent statecraft, political ambitions, and complicity in imperial decisions.
No technological miracles or effortlessly incompetent opposition.
Authorial change requests are authoritative; editorial implementations beyond them remain proposals.
Keep the current master storyline a continuous affirmative narrative, without comparisons to old manuscript construction; put research and implementation notes in historical_background.md.

Distinguish verified historical events from fictional divergences, particularly Pico-Castro reconciliation, spring 1846 convention, Sloat's delayed response, British debt support and the lawful Puʻuloa lease and illegal 1874–1876 ordinances.
Victoria Kamāmalu is historical, born 1 November 1838; the separate Princess Kaʻiulani is born 1875. CT-VICTORIA-KAMAMALU is retired duplicate provenance of active CT-KAIULANI.
Lot dies December 1872; Victoria succeeds under his designated-heir provision, not an election. Rising and lease in 1874 precede illegal ordinances and 1876 judgment.

Silas’s late-1851 birth and Kiyoshi’s 1859 birth/spring-1858 conception are settled by the supplied master and CR-027. Kalanimoku’s birth after the November 1858 wedding and later-1870s loss are settled; exact birth year and accident remain OPEN.
No automatic assumption that Japan's Perry mission vanishes solely because California has purchased coal contracts.
The 1783 mining ordinances do not settle contested private titles or the rights of Indigenous peoples without state law and negotiation.
Treat 1858—not 1860—as the date of the definitive Edo Treaty; the March 1860 Kanrin Maru voyage is a follow-up visit.

CR-014: Lot retains the Kuhina Nui; no missing-office or personal-countersignature mechanism explains confederal ascent. Enabling authority must follow constitutional-amendment procedures and member ratification.
Demographic, fiscal and military figures in rise_to_power.md are planning assumptions, not verified canon; test them before writing numerical claims as facts.
Do not treat the source file's self-labeled APPROVED tags as proof of separate author decisions where this turn expressly identifies historical or mechanical exceptions.
Distinguish adopted framework from unchosen birthplace, exact legal language, electoral events and statutory dates. Weimar provides a structural comparison, not an in-world source.
Kuhina Nui standing supports participation in regency and succession but does not automatically confer the crown or the later imperial regency.
CR-015 labels are component-specific. Merging records does not turn PROPOSED detail or unvalidated model figures into approved fact.
The Power Timeline controls cadence; CR-015 J1 and later explicit decisions control the named corrections. Earlier dated CR-013 planning text is superseded where cross-referenced.
Distinguish Pacifican core population from Philippine crown, associated Gulf citizens, Chinese revenue administration and sovereign Japanese/Korean partners.
CR-016: preserve retired CT-MARCUS-II identity as provenance, without active father-son command genealogy or silently remapping legacy profiles to Soberanes.
CR-018 fixes the stakeholder endpoint and surviving 1932 order; no Julian self-coup, separate 1914 Emperor Kalanimoku, burning Thalassia or Victoria captivity remains active.

Kalanimoku the lost son and Kahekili / Ikazuchi, the c.1916 heir, are distinct; CT-KALANIMOKU-HEIR is a stable ID, not the current name. Fleet-General Kuroda is Kiyoshi; retain stable legacy IDs as provenance rather than inventing another commander.

Russia never completes its own Pacific through connection; Japan completes the eastern link and terminal, with Chinese ownership of Manchuria. Northern coastal cession occurs in 1921, not 1899 or 1905.

CR-019 OPEN items retain their status except OPEN-019-03 (decided), OPEN-019-09 (superseded by CR-020), and OPEN-019-04 (partly resolved by CR-020). CR-018 section N remains wholly proposed under OPEN-018-18, even where CR-019 refers to its suggested archive and death.

The 1865 armistice/framework and 1867 Western Senate ratification remain distinct. 1919 combined-fleet limits do not create the 1927 common ministries. Victoria is 93–94 in 1932 without a chosen birthday.
CR-020 E governs its earlier draft replacements; B4 is superseded and B15/D final figures replace intermediate model tables. MODEL values never become narrative canon through this merge.
No Gulf membership by 1932, no three-year admission period, no Keawe strike/labor-charter arc or main-story labor registration. Guest permits remain background administration.
The 1932 Gulf oil compact follows the failed 1931 streak, despite older 1931 compact assumptions in source B6/D. B14’s full 1927 Japanese crisis borrowing supersedes B3’s earlier 80% figure.
Replacement workbook checks are reported source results. Its missing bank-by-bank and transport tests remain audit gaps, not resolved failures in the earlier workbook.

CR-021 revision 8 and final K decisions override earlier PROPOSED/OPEN labels inside that attachment. All seventeen OPEN-021 entries are decided; uncapped tongue votes are an express direct author decision in revision 9.

Julian is never styled President; the presidency is a delegated executive function of his Crown. Hayama always hosts the crowns’ Council; reigning Hirohito never visits Thalassia. The Altai secret is withheld.
Noe’s identity, 1886 hānai bargain and official autumn 1888 typhoid account are settled; no culprit is proved. Do not erase medical work or reduce Victoria’s rivalry to jealousy.

Hawaiian Crown land and ʻAha Aliʻi custody are distinct from Realm regulation and county lease administration. The 1914 Act joins crowns and restores legislature and language without reversing the 1876 judgment.

The latest dominance/reserve/stress comparisons are source-reported MODEL values. Do not mix their Union per-person comparator with CR-020’s historical-US comparator or infer a complete new GDP series.

Revision 9: Chichibu is selected, not a candidate. His Pacifican education, Crown honors and outdoorsman reputation show Japan’s Pacifican orientation instead of a British/European career. Avoid inventing particular orders, ranks or summit records.
Nikolayevsk joins Kamchatka and Okhotsk coast as Siberian sovereign territory in 1921. Japanese access requires treaty and creates no automatic base or ownership.
Dawes chooses the rescue/association; Young campaigns for acceptance and endorses as president-elect. Crowns agree renewal at Hayama, ministers sign/exchange at Thalassia.
Foreign Affairs and Finance normally Pacifican is a convention, not a statutory nationality rule; only the at-least-one Japanese minister floor is legal. Reserved squadron ends in 1932.
Noe’s official typhoid account and poisoning testimony remain genuinely unresolved; no culprit is newly selected.
CR-027 replaces fictional Kaiulani with historical Victoria Kamāmalu while retaining stable ID CT-KAIULANI and all legacy profiles. Historical Princess Kaʻiulani, born 1875, is separate.
CR-027: No massacre or Hawaiian throne abeyance. The lease is legal; later ordinances and appointed Council illegal; ignored judgment is 1876. The 1914 Act joins crowns.

CR-027 A22/A27 and the individual B9 echoes remain PROPOSED; A13 approves the settlement’s shape while instrument dates and wording remain PROPOSED. Section D’s questions are not resolved by publication.

23 October integration: source instructions and workbook Canon/Approved metadata do not independently authorize new canon. Preserve local PROPOSED/OPEN/MODEL scopes. Missing CR attachments remain absent originals; excerpt records are clearly identified.

provisional_timeline.event: Elias born c.1824, birthplace open; southern Rocky Mountain upbringing; French veteran mentor; 1837 dispossession; witnesses 1840 Council House Fight; Santa Fe captivity with Caleb in 1841–42; arrives California 1844; aids Castro at Providencia 1845; baptized and naturalized.
Logan born in a Kentucky holler, migrates to California as an adolescent, trains in Carquinez workshops and technical institutions; exact dates open.

Santa Barbara convention declares independent República de California on Pentecost; Pico becomes provisional president. Bilingual English–Spanish founding bargain, civil liberties and public religious freedom.
Bear Flag uprising and Olompali, Sloat hesitation and Collingwood, Stockton standstill, San Pasqual; recognition by Mexico with approximately £3m London debt assumption.

Stanislaus/Mokelumne discoveries and public rush; 1849 Mining Law 5% royalty; mint 1850; border Treaty of Monterey; Vallejo president after 1850; vigilante conflict; Elias gains Mines and Revenue superintendency 1852. Common-law commercial institutions, retained rights and bilingual administration attract immigration and technical enterprise.
Friendships with Alexander, Lot and Manjiro; castaway connections through Satsuma; Walker filibusters blocked; Victoria visits San Francisco; Hawaiian coaling treaty and Shimoda arrangements 1855.

Defense Law 1855, first minister appointment, 1856 second Vigilance Committee suppressed; Confederation of Pacifica declared 31 July 1856 in Honolulu; ratified in September and November; Elias becomes Chancellor. Elected Assembly, state Council and institutional Article XIV assent; English confederal working language with member-language guarantees.
Elias marries Victoria Kamāmalu at Kawaiahaʻo after Edo; Kiyoshi was conceived that spring, before the wedding. Victoria’s knowledge remains OPEN.
Utah War and northern gold rushes; Abe Masahiro dies 1857, Nariakira dies 1858; definitive Treaty of Edo is signed in 1858 under new shogunal order.

Comstock discovery east of border; March 1860 Kanrin Maru visit confirms 1858 Edo treaty; Paiute conflict and Washoe intervention; Victoria organizes Hawaiian opposition that withholds state assent to Article XIV; Carson Convention Pacifica withdrawal.
Fort Sumter; fictional Hawaiian packet crisis; Victoria demands protection; Article XIV and separately limited coercive authorization; late-May activation is the working date.

Deseret accedes 1862–1863; Washoe retaken 1863–1864; Navajo treaty avoids Long Walk, Bear River remains atrocity; Mobile attack fails/Farragut killed February 1865; Lincoln electoral defeat leads to 1865 peace framework, Western line ratified 1867; McClellan route and treaty detail proposed.

Consolidation; Alaska 1867, Midway/Baja proposed; Japan equal alliance 1870–1871; Grant war fails 1870–1871, Sherman convention, Confederate association and fugitive agreement 1871–1872; Greeley wins then dies.
Loss of Elias and Victoria's legitimate son Kalanimoku in accident; Victoria unable to bear more children; exact accident open.

Victoria succeeds Lot without election in December 1872, appoints Ruth, settles September 1873 mutiny and keeps Guard. February 1874 rising has disputed deaths. Lawful fifty-year Puʻuloa lease in 1874; illegal ordinances 1874–1876, appointed Council and schools ordinance. Ruth resigns; 1876 judgment ignored. Exact instruments and March lease date PROPOSED.

Brown/Freedom Act, Gordon presidency 1874–1880, free-womb amendment; Manila 1873 and Spanish sale 1876; family settlement; Satsuma government backed 1877; Marcus I dies Vladivostok February 1878; Ryukyu mediation proposed.
Imperial consolidation, illness and other relationships; Julian born 1886 to physician Kaʻanoe Ward.

Panama treaty/railroad 1880, French works; Sunset 1883; Texas abolition 1884; Customs 1885, Port Hamilton near-war; oil/turbine programmes, Tesla arrives 1884 and electrical institute opens 1886 (CR-020); Chinese massacres prosecuted; no foreign military adventure around succession.

Elias dies; managed succession without civil war; proposed pre-death spring 1887 Truce and one Donner standoff. Julian already adopted/raised successor while mother lives; mother later dies mysteriously.

Regency; selective skilled/family immigration 1888; abolition and Hapa proclamation 1888–1889; canal purchase 1889; statistics/weekly/film; Wounded Knee campaign; Confederate compensation-bond guarantee calls begin in Panic.

Bread March; Victoria brokers Korean neutrality in 1894, Formosa stays Chinese under Pacifican revenue administration; Union gold rescue 1895; Whitney elected 1896, prisoner treaty 1897; Japanese gold facility proposed.

Primorye war: Japan land forces, Pacifica sea/credit, France neutral, China recovers Amur north bank. Virginia/North Carolina rejoin Union; Federal Republic of the Gulf with Texas/Louisiana/Arkansas/Sequoyah. Cuba independent under joint guarantee, Estrada Palma president, Puerto Rico Union. Canal opening target 1900–1902; Britain settlement and network details proposed.

Victoria’s de facto government during Elias’s decline remains proposed. Julian’s 1886 birth/adoption is approved by CR-021. Pre-death spring 1887 Truce remains proposed; Donner responsibility is settled by supplied CR-022: Silas fires at Soberanes and kills Caleb. Soberanes’s name and Carquinez seat are approved. Silas is eldest, Kiyoshi second; no succession civil war.

Kiyoshi, Elias’s second son after Silas, enters Kuroda house in 1886 and founds branch; Kiyonaka keeps main house. Count and Fleet-General in 1907; crown bid 1913–1914 renounced. Dies at Kronstadt in May 1920 (CR-040 K1); maternal and early service details retain labels.

Stakeholder compact renewals proposed in 1897, 1907, 1917; Japanese imperial careers rise. Fourth renewal becomes Pacific Concord in 1927, cured in 1928, with Tokyo domestic institutions retained and common ministries at Thalassia.

Russia occupies China’s Manchurian railway from Transbaikalia; Japan wins 1904–1905 war and refuses Roosevelt’s mediation on Victoria’s advice. Japan holds the Pacific terminal; China owns Manchurian section; exact peace terms/signing place remain qualified.

Korea independent under guarantee after 1905; Qing falls and Pacifica backs Sun. Silas confesses Donner and dies in 1912. Kiyoshi claims crown in 1913, renounces in 1914 for Kuroda queen. The Five stay neutral. Victoria lays down regency and Hawaiian crown in 1915; Julian accedes to both and marries Chiyo; Soberanes retires.
Union neutral. Pacifica fights at sea/in Pacific, finances Entente and brokers the peace. Julian’s credit timing, London raid, Hague terms and Victoria’s commission retain proposed/open status.

CR-040 Stages 3–4 and CR-041 (integrated 29 October 2026): the line seized in one week from 26 May 1918; Kazan held in September 1918; the tri-partite Siberian treaty (Komuch, Siberia, Alash) of 4–6 August 1918, ratified 10 September; the Omsk coup fails; Perm December 1918; the Volga battle of June 1919 with Vance on the Zelenodolsk bridge; Nizhny December 1919; Tula, the Oka, Moscow, Petrograd, Kotelnich and Kronstadt in 1920 as CR-040 Stages 3–4; the Tomsk vote of 1921 brings Siberia into federal Russia and Alash with it, unasked. British debt settlement, Japanese earthquake rescue and union crisis proposed. Chiang succeeds Sun; Zhang Zuolin assassinated; Zhang Xueliang holds Manchuria. Inspectorate returned on proposed defense bargain; Formosan administration retained.

Depression; Pacifican moratorium, gold lending, bank support and second Union rescue; detailed settlement mechanics qualified. 1931 Manchurian plot stopped; May 1932 coup fails; overseas Japanese commands become common. Vance’s revised arc remains OPEN-018-18.

Pacific order survives and leads. Victoria brokers Keawe’s Lands and Waters Charter; Chronicler records triumph and cost. Thalassia Conference and archive mechanics remain qualified; no Gulf membership. Owen D. Young elected November, FDR cooperates; Young takes office 1933.
Development Fund and savings/development finance support Polytechnic champions; Crown stakes depend on charters or patent licences; standing public debt supports investment and central banking.
Guest-worker programme supplements skilled and family routes; quotas, employer levy, protected contracts and eventual residence remain background to the main story.
Pacifica Steel buys Carnegie 1901; Roosevelt’s emulation and containment response starts 1903, full force 1910; turbine capital ships 1903; Pacifican moving assembly line 1911.
Living Bay sewage diversion, watershed protection and fishpond restoration; Kāneʻohe Bay marine reserve and Moku o Loʻe station 1923. Thalassia stands on windward Oʻahu.

The whole order overtakes Union money output as partners grow; 1932 Pacifica-only nominal crossing is a resented headline while Union real output remains larger. Union joins fleet limits; emulation and containment continue.

Monterey common government until 1885; lawful 1865 Enabling Law/life Providentorship. Lawful Puʻuloa lease 1874; illegal 1874–1876 ordinances and Council; ignored 1876 judgment. Constitution of Realm legal in form, Truce extra-legal then organic law. Victoria Queen from 1872 and Regent from 1887; the Five run chartered estates.

Thalassia decision 1875, Pearl works 1875–85, Pali tunnel/channel 1876–82, cable 1879, offices move 1885. Noe qualifies 1884, physician 1885, health board and Julian birth/adoption 1886, dies contested typhoid 1888; registers found Office of Public Measures.

Plural and uncapped tongue votes, county grades and certification; Victoria extends Noe’s health work. Julian’s 1907 majority does not end regency. 1914 Act establishes Pacifican Crown, joins existing Hawaiian crown, dissolves Council and restores legislature/schools/language; Julian heir, accedes in 1915.

Polytechnic of Formosa opens 1906, Japanese school/joint board 1928, Sino-Pacifican foundation 1928–29. Formosan Revenue Convention becomes Concord administration with Chinese-commissioned Japanese deputy.
